audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for unjust steward, Mammon, law/prophets, divorce saying, rich man and Lazarus, Abraham's bosom, Hades/depths, reversal and Moses/prophets warning.

verses.restored: He also said to the disciples, A certain rich person had a steward, and this one was accused to him as squandering his possessions.

familiar.text: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.

verses.restored: Calling him, he said, What is this I hear about you? Give the account of your stewardship, for you are no longer able to steward.

familiar.text: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.

verses.restored: The steward said within himself, What shall I do, because my lord is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.

familiar.text: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.

verses.restored: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from stewardship, people may receive me into their houses.

familiar.text: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

verses.restored: Calling each one of his lord's debtors, he said to the first, How much do you owe my lord?

familiar.text: So he called every one of his lord’s debtors unto him, and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?

verses.restored: He said, A hundred baths of oil. He said to him, Take your bill, sit quickly, and write fifty.

familiar.text: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.

verses.restored: Then to another he said, And you, how much do you owe? He said, A hundred cors of wheat. He says to him, Take your bill and write eighty.

familiar.text: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore.

verses.restored: The lord praised the steward of injustice because he acted shrewdly; for the children of this age are more shrewd toward their own generation than the children of light.

familiar.text: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.

verses.restored: And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by means of Mammon of injustice, so that when it fails, they may receive you into age-long tents.

familiar.text: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.

verses.restored: The one trustworthy in least is trustworthy also in much, and the one unjust in least is unjust also in much.

familiar.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

verses.restored: If then you have not become trustworthy with unjust Mammon, who will entrust to you the true?

familiar.text: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

verses.restored: If you have not become trustworthy with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?

familiar.text: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?

verses.restored: No household servant is able to serve two lords; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold fast to one and despise the other. You are not able to serve the Divine and Mammon.

familiar.text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

verses.restored: The Pharisees, being lovers of silver, heard all these things and were ridiculing him.

familiar.text: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.

verses.restored: He said to them, You are the ones justifying yourselves before humans, but the Divine knows your hearts; because what is high among humans is an abomination before the Divine.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

verses.restored: The Law and the Prophets were until John; from then the good news of the reign of the Divine is announced, and everyone is pressing into it.

familiar.text: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.

verses.restored: It is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the Law to fall.

familiar.text: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.

verses.restored: Everyone releasing his wife and marrying another commits adultery, and the one marrying a woman released from a husband commits adultery.

familiar.text: Whosoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery.

verses.restored: There was a certain rich person, clothed in purple and fine linen, making merry splendidly every day.

familiar.text: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:

verses.restored: A certain poor person named Lazarus had been laid at his gate, covered with sores,

familiar.text: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,

verses.restored: longing to be filled from the things falling from the rich person's table; even the dogs came and licked his sores.

familiar.text: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.

verses.restored: It happened that the poor person died and was carried away by the messengers to Abraham's bosom. The rich person also died and was buried.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;

verses.restored: In Hades/depths, being in torment, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham from far away and Lazarus in his bosom.

familiar.text: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

verses.restored: He called out, Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in anguish in this flame.

familiar.text: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.

verses.restored: Abraham said, Child, remember that you received your good things in your life, and Lazarus likewise harmful things; now here he is comforted, and you are in anguish.

familiar.text: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

verses.restored: Besides all these things, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, so that those wanting to pass from here to you are not able, nor may they cross from there to us.

familiar.text: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.

verses.restored: He said, Then I ask you, father, that you send him to my father's house,

familiar.text: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:

verses.restored: for I have five brothers, so that he may warn them, lest they also come into this place of anguish.

familiar.text: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

verses.restored: Abraham says, They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them.

familiar.text: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

verses.restored: But he said, No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will turn/realign.

familiar.text: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.

verses.restored: He said to him, If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
